proposed_fix.description: Confirm whether the ts-auth-service slowdown and packet loss come from its node or pod networking or from resource pressure, then mitigate with gated, reversible actions such as restarting or rescheduling a single replica.
steps: Compare ts-auth-service pod and node metrics (CPU throttling, memory, network drops/retransmits, conntrack usage) against the time of the latency rise seen in E1/E4.
Inspect the elevated socket count (E4, +30%) on ts-auth-service for connection buildup, such as many TIME_WAIT or retransmitting connections.
Check whether the latency is confined to pods on one node; if so, cordon that node (reversible with uncordon) after human approval.
If one replica is degraded, delete that single pod so it reschedules on another node, only after confirming other replicas are healthy and serving.
If conntrack usage on the node is near its limit, move some pods off the node as a gated step; only consider raising the limit after approval and with a documented rollback.
After each action, watch ts-auth-service latency-50/90 and the downstream ts-inside-payment-service errors and ts-ui-dashboard latency (E1) for recovery.
preconditions: Confirm that ts-auth-service has more than one healthy replica and that a pod disruption budget or capacity allows removing one.
Verify the node's conntrack, packet drop and CPU/memory numbers to establish that the node is the likely cause before cordoning or moving anything.
Get on-call approval before any cordon, pod deletion or node setting change.
Record current replica placement and node sysctl values so they can be restored.
proposed_fix.rollback: Uncordon the node, restore the original conntrack limit and any other node settings from the recorded values, and scale or reschedule pods back to their original placement if the change did not help or made things worse.
